skill.name: screen-reader-testing
skill.description: Test web applications with screen readers including VoiceOver, NVDA, and JAWS. Use when validating screen reader compatibility, debugging accessibility issues, or ensuring assistive technology support.
skill.summary: Guides manual screen reader testing for web accessibility across major assistive technologies.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by accessibility examples and Markdown code spans. No malicious intent, credential handling, shell execution, or prompt injection was found in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 391 checks the JavaScript KeyboardEvent key value for Tab inside a focus trap example. This is not a certificate, private key, or credential file reference.
Line 407 checks the KeyboardEvent key value for Escape in modal keyboard handling. The token key is an event property, not sensitive certificate material.
Line 475 switches on e.key for tab interface keyboard navigation. The example handles arrow and home keys and does not reference certificate or key files.
Line 27 lists TalkBack as a screen reader platform in an accessibility support table. It is not collecting host, network, or system reconnaissance data.
Line 160 is an HTML example showing a visible form error message. It does not perform reconnaissance or access system information.
Line 164 is an accessible form error example using role alert. It is static instructional markup, not system reconnaissance behavior.
Line 266 asks testers to enter invalid form data during accessibility testing. This is normal QA guidance and does not probe system configuration.
Line 29 uses Markdown backticks around a resource file path. It is not Ruby backtick syntax and does not execute a shell command.
Line 33 uses Markdown inline code formatting for the implementation playbook path. There is no executable code or command invocation.

content.value_statement: Screen reader regressions can hide behind visual checks. This skill gives practical testing steps for VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, and TalkBack.
actual_capabilities: Guides manual testing with VoiceOver on macOS and iOS.
Provides NVDA, JAWS, and TalkBack command references.
Supplies checklists for landmarks, headings, forms, tables, and dynamic updates.
Shows accessible patterns for modals, live regions, tab interfaces, and form errors.
Suggests debugging checks for accessible names, roles, states, and visibility.
limitations: Does not automate screen reader execution or capture speech output.
Does not replace testing by users who rely on assistive technology.
Does not cover every screen reader version, browser combination, or OS setting.
Requires access to the target app and the relevant screen reader software.

use_cases.title: Check Frontend Regressions
use_cases.description: Test a changed dialog, form, or tab interface before release.

use_cases.title: Build Accessibility QA Plans
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable checklist for VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, and TalkBack coverage.

use_cases.title: Review Shared Components
use_cases.description: Verify that reusable components expose useful names, roles, states, and focus behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Page Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation for one web page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a screen reader testing checklist for this page. Cover page load, navigation, links, buttons, forms, dynamic content, and tables.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for forms and validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this form workflow for screen reader testing. Include labels, required fields, error announcements, invalid input, focus movement, and recovery steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Dynamic Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for interactive UI behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan screen reader tests for a modal, live region, and tab interface. Include expected announcements, keyboard movement, and focus return checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Release Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cross-screen-reader QA plan for this release. Prioritize browser pairs, test flows, evidence to collect, and unresolved risk.

output_examples.input: Request: Test a checkout form with NVDA.
output_examples.output: Checklist covering initial load, landmark navigation, field labels, required state, invalid email, error announcement, and focus recovery.

output_examples.input: Request: Review a modal dialog for VoiceOver.
output_examples.output: Test steps for opening the dialog, confirming its name, trapping focus, closing with Escape, and returning focus to the trigger.

output_examples.input: Request: Build a release accessibility test plan.
output_examples.output: Prioritized matrix covering NVDA with Firefox, VoiceOver with Safari, JAWS with Chrome, and mobile TalkBack smoke checks.

best_practices: Test with real screen readers before relying on automated accessibility results.
Cover both browse and focus modes when validating interactive controls.
Document browser, operating system, screen reader, and version for each result.
anti_patterns: Treating one screen reader result as proof that every platform works.
Testing only successful flows and skipping validation errors or loading states.
Adding ARIA before checking whether semantic HTML solves the problem.

faq.question: Does this skill run screen readers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides manual testing guidance, checklists, and expected behavior.

faq.question: Which screen readers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, TalkBack, and Windows Narrator at a practical level.

faq.question: Can this replace automated accessibility tools?
faq.answer: No. Use it alongside automated checks, keyboard testing, and semantic HTML review.

faq.question: Is it useful for mobile accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TalkBack gestures and VoiceOver coverage for iOS workflows.

faq.question: What evidence should testers collect?
faq.answer: Record the tested platform, browser, screen reader, version, flow, result, and any failed announcement.

faq.question: Does it teach ARIA implementation patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for forms, modals, live regions, and tab interfaces.
